# Does your package.json "exports" map point at files that actually exist?

> Paste your package.json and a listing of the files you actually publish and see every literal target in the "exports" map that points at a file that doesn't exist -- the cause of ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED and Cannot find module right after npm install. Free, runs entirely in your browser, nothing is uploaded.

It also flags wildcard targets that reach no listed file and targets Node refuses (no leading "./", another package's name, a ".." segment: ERR_INVALID_PACKAGE_TARGET), and its resolver names the file `import "my-lib/feature"` or `require("#internal")` reaches under any conditions, using Node 22's algorithm, checked against Node itself on more than 85,000 generated cases with no disagreement (resolve.diff.test.mjs). CLI: `node cli.mjs check`, `node cli.mjs resolve <specifier> [--require] [--conditions=a,b]`.

Free and open source (MIT). Results are estimates from the numbers typed in, not legal, tax, financial or professional advice.
